newsitem.title: USA: Royal Oak expands Ontario gold reserves.
newsitem.headline: Royal Oak expands Ontario gold reserves.

text.p: Royal Oak Mines Inc said on Wednesday it has expanded its mineral resource at its gold properties in the Timmins area of Northern Ontario.
The Kirkland, Washington-based company said its Timmins and Matachewan land positions contain about 7.3 million ounces of gold in 132 million tons of ore at a grade of 0.056 ounces per tonne.
The additional reserves are an increase of 2.81 million ounces over the 1995 year-end published resource at the Ontario division, the company said in a statement.
The increase will boost production at the Pamour Mine.
The company said it is currently putting together a feasibility study to design an expanded open pit and determine the future of underground and open pit production at Pamour.
The expansion means the Pamour Mill will be expanded from its current 4,000 tons per day capacity to 15,000 tons per day, Royal Oak said.
Production by late 1998 is expected to be about 300,000 ounces per year from the Timmins and Matachewan camps cash costs of production under US$225 per ounce.

"The success of our exploration programs in the Timmins camp has demonstrated the potential which exists on our large land position on the Destor-Porcupine fault, one of Canada's most prolific gold producing areas," Royal Oak president Margaret Witte said in a statement.
